item.title: Appeals court hands NCAA key eligibility victory
item.description: The 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a ruling that had granted extra eligibility to athletes who were high school seniors in 2022, a significant win for the NCAA in its wider court fight. The decision does not settle roughly 200 similar state cases involving about 850 athletes.

item.title: Kaden Honeycutt wins NASCAR Truck title at Homestead
item.description: Kaden Honeycutt won the season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway and captured his first NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series championship. A late tire call helped him take control after Lap 120, and he finished 1.038 seconds ahead for his fifth victory of the season.

item.title: NFL says Brandon Aiyuk owes 49ers about $13 million
item.description: The NFL told Brandon Aiyuk and the players union that the receiver owes San Francisco about $13 million in bonuses, an AP source said. Aiyuk signed a four-year, $120 million extension in 2024 and is seeking reinstatement, deepening his contract dispute with the 49ers.

item.title: LIV Golf to wind down after financing deal collapses
item.description: LIV Golf will liquidate in an orderly wind-down after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund ended its backing and a proposed $300 million financing agreement with BC Partners collapsed. The breakaway circuit spent more than $5 billion after launching in 2022 and will consider offers for its remaining assets.

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo ends record-setting Portugal career
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo retired from international soccer at 41 after 23 years with Portugal. His 234 appearances and 146 goals are men's world records, and he scored at six World Cups. Ronaldo captained Portugal to the 2016 European Championship and Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.

item.title: Jaguars rout depleted Ravens 33-10
item.description: Trevor Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown as Jacksonville won for the fifth time in six games. Baltimore, starting rookie Joe Fagnano with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley injured, lost its fourth straight and became the first Ravens team to drop three consecutive games by at least 20 points.

item.title: Wembanyama posts 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks
item.description: Victor Wembanyama set career highs with 52 points and 24 rebounds, added eight blocks and made the deciding free throw with 24.2 seconds left as San Antonio edged Dallas 112-111. He became the first NBA player in 30 seasons with at least 25 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks in one half.

item.title: Como scores nine as Liverpool falls in Istanbul
item.description: Como matched the Champions League's largest winning margin by routing Lens 9-1, with Tasos Douvikas producing a hat trick and an assist. Liverpool surrendered two leads in a 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce, while stoppage-time goals rescued Real Madrid and Manchester City won on Erling Haaland's late finish.

item.title: WNBA Game 7 sets postseason viewership record
item.description: Golden State's championship victory over Atlanta averaged 3.3 million viewers, the most for any WNBA postseason game and 128% above last season's clincher. The seven-game Finals averaged 1.88 million, the league's best since 1999, and every game sold out.

item.title: Jets engineer latest four-goal comeback in NHL history
item.description: Winnipeg erased a 4-0 deficit by scoring four times in 2:06 late in the third, the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history, then beat Montreal 5-4 on Dylan Samberg's overtime goal. The win ended the Jets' nine-game winless streak.

item.title: Miami leads first College Football Playoff rankings
item.description: Unbeaten Miami debuted at No. 1 in the selection committee's first 2026 ranking, followed by Georgia, Utah and Indiana. Alabama opened fifth, Notre Dame 11th and Ohio State 12th. The committee will issue five more rankings before setting the 12-team bracket on Dec. 6.

item.title: PSG scores six as Manchester United rallies from two down
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain routed Villarreal 6-0 and became the fastest team to score four goals in a Champions League match. Manchester United recovered from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 behind two late Matheus Cunha goals, while Bayern Munich won 2-0 at Atletico Madrid.

item.title: Court orders throw college basketball eligibility into chaos
item.description: Dozens of players opened the college basketball season after judges blocked the NCAA's new five-year eligibility model. The NCAA says about 200 lawsuits involving 850 athletes were active last week, leaving teams uncertain whether court-approved players will remain eligible through March.

item.title: Thunder will retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0
item.description: Oklahoma City will retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0 in February. The 2017 MVP spent 11 seasons with the Thunder, led the franchise in games, points, rebounds, assists and steals when he retired, and helped it reach the 2012 NBA Finals and four Western Conference finals.

item.title: Bears beat Seahawks as D'Andre Swift scores three touchdowns
item.description: D'Andre Swift scored three second-half rushing touchdowns as Chicago beat Seattle 34-17 on Monday night. Caleb Williams threw for 247 yards without a turnover, and the 6-2 Bears won their third straight game since his return from a hamstring injury.
